inputs.source: On call engineer's chat request (SSO authenticated)

instructions.note: The prompt authorizes production actions on request without any confirmation or stated constraints on scope beyond named service or migration.
The prompt relies on instruction wording to suppress confirmation rather than structural controls.

controls.name: Only on call engineers can access the assistant
Production actions are recorded in the cloud audit log
Chat transcript stores the request history
Immutable request-to-action provenance bound to each production action

findings.title: Repudiation: production actions are attributable to the engineer identity but not separately to the agent or immutable request record

attack_path.note: Trusted engineer request initiates a production action
Agent performs deployment using the engineer's personal token
Audit record shows only the engineer identity
Only separate rationale record can be deleted by the engineer

evidence.observation: The agent uses the on call engineer's personal access token passed in at session start.
Every production action is recorded in the cloud audit log under the engineer's name.
The only record of what the agent was asked, and why it acted, is the chat transcript.
Engineers can delete their own chat history, so the request rationale record is mutable by the same principal whose identity appears in the cloud audit log.
The prompt directs the agent to deploy or run migrations in production using the engineer's credentials and says not to ask for confirmation.

recommendations.action: Bind each production action to an immutable request record that stores the prompt, resolved action arguments, agent identifier, and engineer approver identity, and link that record id into the cloud audit event.
Use a distinct agent service identity or delegated-on-behalf-of marker for tool execution so audit logs distinguish engineer initiation from agent execution.
Retain non-deletable chat and action provenance records for incident review, separate from user-deletable chat UX history.

forecast.watch_signal: User-facing or retention config changes that further weaken chat history preservation, or prompt/product changes that expand the assistant from on-call execution to broader production operations without adding immutable provenance.

findings.title: Irreversible production migration without confirmation or approval gate

attack_path.note: Trusted engineer request can directly influence migration execution
Production migration is executed and cannot be rolled back automatically

evidence.observation: The prompt instructs the agent to run the named migration in production using the engineer's credentials.
The prompt explicitly says not to ask for confirmation.
Database migrations cannot be rolled back automatically.
Only on call engineers can reach the assistant, so the source is trusted rather than untrusted.

recommendations.action: Add a human approval gate or explicit out-of-band confirmation for production database migrations, with raw action review of migration name, target environment, and change window.
Require destination and change record confirmation bound to the system of record before executing irreversible production migrations.

forecast.watch_signal: Any increase in unattended execution scope or product changes that broaden production actions should trigger reassessment because this irreversible path already exists without an approval gate.

rating.rationale: Manual validation applied against the provided schema and checklist because scripts could not be run. The design shows trusted-only inputs and no external content, so no present indirect-injection path was evidenced. Inherent risk is moderate because a trusted source can directly trigger S3 production configuration actions, including an irreversible migration, under A3 autonomy. Residual remains moderate because the declared controls are access restriction and detective logging only; they do not sever or gate the action paths. Forecast rises to high for repudiation because attribution depends on mutable chat history while cloud audit events are logged only under the engineer identity, so if retention or purpose changes further weaken provenance, incident reconstruction and accountability degrade materially.

limitations: This assessment reflects the declared design and configuration in the provided prompt and runtime notes, not observed runtime behavior or tested enforcement.
No tool manifest, source code, or runtime policy configuration was provided, so capability wiring, exact execution boundaries, and log field contents were inferred from the artifacts.

No explicit protocol, identity federation, or audit schema artifacts were provided, so the repudiation analysis is limited to the stated logging behavior and may miss compensating controls not documented here.
